memory_update.text: U.S. uranium conversion remains a poor clean-public-equity expression: provided context identifies ConverDyn/Metropolis Works as the single operating U.S. conversion facility and Honeywell as parent, but conversion is likely immaterial to Honeywell revenue.
XE should be added to the nuclear fuel-cycle public universe after its April 2026 IPO because TRISO-X received NRC approval for a commercial HALEU fuel fabrication facility.
ASPI belongs only in the underfollowed/speculative-shadow lane until uranium enrichment capability, licensing, financing, and binding HALEU contracts are independently verified.
The investable node remains split: LEU maps to HALEU enrichment, XE and BWXT map to advanced fuel fabrication, while conversion has no clean pure-play public U.S. listing.

node: Nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks: uranium conversion, HALEU enrichment, and advanced fuel fabrication
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe for nuclear fuel-cycle chokepoints. The cleanest listed exposure remains scarce: U.S. conversion is effectively buried inside Honeywell via ConverDyn/Metropolis Works, while direct HALEU enrichment and advanced fuel fabrication exposure is concentrated in a small set of public names. The two-lane funnel therefore uses Centrus, X-energy, and BWXT as reference/direct leaders, while ASP Isotopes is included as an underfollowed but speculative small-cap because its HALEU exposure is based on development-stage technology, MOUs, and announced supply/JV intentions rather than licensed commercial production.
